reason: The capillary sleeves explicitly show an inner surface for the endothelial lining, so these pieces can form the exchange vessels.
expectation: The lining should fit inside the sleeves to form capillaries.

alternatives.reason: The lining could also form the inner surface of an artery.

effect: The endothelial lining and sleeves formed the capillary bed, establishing the exchange portion of the route.
reaction: The thin-wall connection to exchange is clear and satisfying.
reason: The arterial wall needs an endothelial inner lining to form an artery.
expectation: The lining and arterial wall should form an artery.

alternatives.reason: A vein also needs an endothelial lining.

effect: The lining and arterial wall formed arterial vessels, with an elastic wall that stretches and recoils.
reaction: The pulse-and-rest comparison makes the wall’s role clearer.
reason: The venous wall also needs an endothelial lining to make the return vessels.
expectation: The lining and venous wall should form venous vessels.

alternatives.reason: The artery and capillary bed could be connected first.

effect: The endothelial lining and venous wall formed thin-walled veins, completing the three vessel types needed for the route.
reaction: The vein’s wide, thin-walled structure is clear, though its function has not yet been explained.
reason: The pocket-shaped valve folds belong inside the vein and should help direct returning blood.
expectation: The folds should form valves inside the veins that limit backflow.

alternatives.reason: I could connect the outgoing vessels to the exchange bed first.

effect: The valves completed venous return, showing how muscle compression and valves help move blood toward the heart.
reaction: The muscle-and-valve illustration clarifies how backflow is limited.
reason: Arterial vessels should lead into the capillary bed before blood returns through veins.
expectation: The arteries should connect to the capillary network.

alternatives.reason: The capillary bed also needs a connection to the return vessels.

effect: The arteries now connect through arterioles to the capillary network; the remaining route is venous return.
reaction: The parallel capillary branches make the connection to broad tissue coverage clear.
reason: Connecting venous return should complete the route from arteries through capillaries and back.
expectation: The capillary network should connect to veins carrying blood back toward the heart.

effect: Connecting venous return completed the systemic vessel network and the chapter goal.
reaction: The completed route clearly brings the vessel roles together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the venous valves was most worthwhile: the planned picture connects muscle compression, forward flow and prevention of backflow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled veins was relatively repetitive after lining the artery, and that result did not yet explain the vein's function.

surprise.text: The planned venous-return picture made the role of contracting limb muscles in moving blood back toward the heart more explicit than I expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each vessel component had an identifiable place in the route.

continue.text: I would continue: the vessel constructions linked their structures to exchange and blood return, though the decisions themselves were fairly predictable.
